evidence.description: The shared singleton is declared using nonisolated(unsafe).

candidates.explanation: The 'shared' singleton instance is declared as 'nonisolated(unsafe)', which bypasses Swift's concurrency safety checks. Since the class manages published properties and interacts with shared services, this could lead to data races if accessed from multiple threads.
candidates.title: Potential Thread Safety Issue with Shared Singleton

evidence.description: Use of nonisolated(unsafe) for static properties.
Use of Task blocks within non-isolated methods to update state.

candidates.explanation: The class mixes 'nonisolated(unsafe)' static properties, 'Task' blocks for asynchronous work, and '@MainActor' annotated methods. This inconsistency can make it difficult to reason about which thread is accessing shared state, especially when 'Task' blocks are spawned from non-isolated contexts.
candidates.title: Mixed Concurrency Models

evidence.description: Nested @MainActor Task inside an @MainActor annotated method.

candidates.explanation: The method 'handleUserProfileUpdate' is already annotated with '@MainActor', but it contains an internal 'Task { @MainActor in ... }' block. This is redundant as the entire method is already guaranteed to run on the main actor.
candidates.title: Redundant MainActor Dispatch

candidates.explanation: The 'animateBalanceChange' method uses hardcoded 'asyncAfter' delays (1.0 and 3.0 seconds). Hardcoded magic numbers for UI timing can lead to a poor user experience if the app's performance varies or if the UI requirements change.
candidates.title: Hardcoded Animation Delays
